The Sims 3 is really fun and addictive! Still, it is important that buyers be aware of what they're actually getting prior to investing in this game. If you do not do a little research ahead of time, you may end up feeling disappointed once you begin to play. 

The Sims has always been a franchise built around DLC. If you are trying out Sims for the first time and you decide to only purchase the base game (to experiment and save some money), keep in mind that you will not be able to do many of the things you probably have seen in player videos and previews. That being said - I would suggest reading through the descriptions of the available DLC prior to making your purchase. Choose what might be worth investing in based upon what you hoped to get out of this game. 

For instance - are you simply looking to play around with one character - walk him/her through their daily life, get a job, climb the career ladder, etc? If so, the base game may work out just fine for you. If you're looking for more, you may want to choose a bundle, or purchase the game with some DLC, right away. Still, think carefully before spending your money. DLC for The Sims is relatively costly. If you know you would enjoy playing with cats, dogs, and horses, and engaging in outdoor seasonal activities - the main bundle (with generations, pets, and seasons) may be worth the expense. But, if you're more interested in traveling the world, creating vampires and witches, or living the college life, you're probably better off skipping the bundle and just buying The Sims 3 plus one additional DLC that meets your needs. 

In short - The Sims 3 is a great game - but you may be disappointed, or end up spending more than you'd like for content you do not need or care about, if you do not do some research before making your purchase.

If you experience crashing after running the game multiple times, please download the Mod "Sims 3 GPU Add-On Support" from Nexus Mods; as the description says "This is an easy app that adds most of the GPU after year 2013 to the list and its rules."

Next google Nraas and go to their website, the orange and white will blind you a bit but once adjusted look at the right of the page at the column of orange and yellow mods and download at minimum: 

ErrorTrap = ( intended to catch and correct data corruption errors that can render a save-game unloadable)
Overwatch = (( act as a periodic clean up system for correcting errors and eliminating junk)Winton))
Saver = (prompts the user to save after a given amount of play-time. By default, the mod will wake after 30 minutes)

Place everything into your sims 3 mods folder in your documents folder (c:user/YOURNAME/Documents/Electronic Arts/The Sims 3/Mods) 
If you don't have one; make a folder called Mods, and in the Mods folder create another one called "Packages"
Download a Sims 3 Resource.Cfg File and place it in the Mods folder. If you get any errors remove the old resource file and remove any extra files that may be unnecessarily populating your Mods folder.

To Install Mods download it to your computer, open/unzip the file to get the .package file (macs will need Keka for extracting i've heard), and place them in your packages folder. If its not recognized or doesn't show up at the main menu with its little pop-up that lists mods installed; then it may be better to have it inside the Mods file itself, instead of your packages file. Alternatively make a cheat savegame and cheat your way to being able to check if the mod is working.
I.E. More inventions on the inventing table at higher skill levels, so cheating to a higher skill level to see if your sim is able to even craft the custom content downloaded. (Old games have finicky solutions for problems, and it can just not list mods you have for no reason so a cheat save after every batch of new mods added can be a fun way to check if everything is working well together.)

Everything else on their website is up to you to personally choose for your game/experience (especially if you're a coomer), but the listed ones earlier massively improved my own experience and should help in you preventing any save loss or frame dips long term. Overwatch especially, since it will turn off active speakers, Tvs and other toggle-ables that might be taking up excess resources in the games system.
The game is a resource hog even now, so if you have everything ultra don't be suprised if you're suddenly looking down a barrel of a Throttling gun.

Let us start off like this.

Now, right off the bat, if you try to launch this game and it immediately crashes even after downloading the ".net" it requests. Give up and request a refund. I'm serious. Your system is NOT compatible not matter what forums you follow.

I was stubborn (and extremely dumb) and found answers from a forum explaining that if I wanted the game to work past the menu screen that I needed to open TaskManager after launching the game, and to disable all CPU's except for CPU 0. That worked and I got my hopes up. I went through the character creation screen excited, I picked my house to finally begin excited, but before I actually played I exited the game and bought my favorite DLCS thinking I had solved all my problems and I wanted the gameplay to now be what I remembered.

Bought the dlcs, downloaded them, started the game. Realized my save files were all corrupted, figured it was because I bought a few dlcs, I shrugged it off because I had no plans on getting anymore, so deleting my old saves and uninstalling and reinstalling wasn't a problem for me. I went through character creation, made a character and a cat, picked a world, and started the game. Except when I went to save it immediately after I finished character creation and selected a world, an error 16 notify appeared. Concerned I saw someone say if you save using "Save As" it'd be fine. So I did that and it saved and I figured that was it.

Except when I clicked my save the error persisted. I deleted all old save files, all corrupted files, the error never left. Not just for my save, but for ALL the DLC worlds I had JUST bought were no longer playable.
I tried unsyncing the one-drive like someone suggested. Nothing was working. Absolutely nothing. Every aspect of my game was completely corrupted. Everything I foolishly just bought was corrupted and unplayable. Those 2.7 hours of playtime you see above my head aren't real. I spent at MAX an hour and maybe 20 minutes playing this game in total. You wanna know why it says that? Because even after closing the game, it still runs. So while I exited the game and was looking through forums trying to figure out how to fix it, Steam was recording my playtime as active. I was so confused, even pressing stop wouldn't immediately shut it down, I had to open up Task Manager and manually turn it off. 

Don't be stubborn. Steam is unlikely to give refunds past the 2 hour mark. And the game REFUSING to load and properly shut down ate up so much of my opportunity for a refund, I'll be LUCKY if Steam gives me a grace and issues me a refund. If any of those beginning steps happen to you, shut the game down in Task Manager and issue for a refund IMMEDIATELY. It's your only chance. As a matter of fact, don't get this game at all. It will NOT run naturally. And even if you do get it run it will NOT save your save files OR your world files. Nothing you do will ever be permanent, not even the worlds you buy if you do decide to get a DLC.

how i've been able to run the game;
1. open Sims 3 launcher
2. open task manager
3. in task manager, locate 'Sims3LauncherW'
4. open details
5. right click 'Sims3LauncherW' -> set affinity
6. deselect all CPU cores. select CPU 1 only
7. press play
8. in task manager Details, 'TS3W.exe' should now appear
9. right click 'TS3W.exe' -> set affinity
10. select all cores
game will now run. you have to do this each time, though it goes pretty fast once you get the hang of it. hope this helps.

Before you download any mods just make sure you know how to download CC (custom content), and make sure that you know the basics. Your cc folder should have three files in it, packages, overrides, resource.cfg. You can download the frameworksetup file from the internet, specifically from a website called Mod the Sims. After that, just rename it to "Mods" and you should move it to documents > Electronic Arts > Sims 3. That's it. CC is great, and it allows you to get so many cool stuff in the game such as clothes, hairs, skins and all that. You can also download custom worlds, houses, etc. one of the most well-known websites for CC is The Sims Resource, and it has a lot of things for you to download, just make sure you download stuff mainly from featured artists, since a lot of CC can be bugged when you get it into the game. 

Overall, I do recommend the game, and it's totally worth it.

There is so much content and freedom in this game that it's actually insane. 
Sure, there are many bugs and performance issues, but that can mostly be solved by installing a few essential mods and clearing your cache/save file from time to time. 

The open world in this game is exactly why it feels so amazing and alive. It's so nice being able to spend time outside your home and seamlessly go to the gym, go out for a coffee, go to the movie theater, go horse riding, grocery shopping, take part in eating contests, local festivals, etc... The Sims 4 has some of that but it's plagued with a tedious loading system and lacks the aforementioned open world system. This system is the reason why it's so easy to juggle a large family in The Sims 3. There is also simply more content in this game and there are more things to do gameplay-wise. The Sims 3 is a great life simulator, whereas the Sims 4 just has a great character creator and is a great house building sim.

Sadly as we already know, there won't be a new Sims game any time soon, so for the time being, I recommend you skip The Sims 4, and just play this old but amazing masterpiece.

In my opinion, one of the greatest casual games of all time, and the greatest Sims game ever made.

However, this game comes with a [b]major[/b] defect: the publisher does not care about the game, at all. Since this game is published by Electronic Arts, that's probably not surprising. There are 2 things in particular that stick out about the way EA has handled this game that you absolutely need to know if you're planning on purchasing it.

1. This release of the game has a massive flaw where NPCs and vehicles will get stuck, yet continue to try and pathfind. Over time this creates a build up of lag that renders your world/save file unplayable. It doesn't matter how careful you are, this is unavoidable, and the longer you play the more likely it becomes.
      The game has a 'living world' where NPCs will walk around and live their own lives independent of the players household, with no load zones. This feature is incredible and unique to this entry, but it also causes the severe lag problem. Luckily, modding this game is very simple. NRaas Overwatch and ErrorTrap mods fix these issues and are necessary to prevent the mentioned problem. These are the only 2 mods that you absolutely have to have.


2. The paywall locked content. Its absurd that EA is still charging 20 bucks per DLC for this game that came out in 2009. You can get a 'decent' price on the full bundle (when its discounted!), but you have to look specifically for it and wait for a heavy discount. 
       Even if you buy the discounted bundle, guess what? EA still found a way to squeeze even more transactions into this game. There's a separate Sims store where you can buy all kinds of in-game stuff. And people, this might be the most embarrassing thing of all.

      The Sims store uses a "Sims Points' currency, which you CANNOT purchase from their official website. After looking around for a bit, solutions were mentioned that involved downloading EAs desktop launcher (pass), linking your steam account, navigating to the game, going to the DLC tab, buying point- No, just don't do that, it's the dumbest thing imaginable. 
      There are somewhere around 1000 items on the points store, and some of the best hairstyles, clothing and furniture are on there (because of course they are.) The prices are absurd, and EA expects you to do an equally absurd little dance just for the privilege of being able to buy these items. Thankfully, its extremely easy to find all of these items for free online.

This game is actually incredible, doubly so when you have access to all of its content. But it is not worth the price EA is asking for it. I felt dirty handing such a large chunk of money to a company that obviously doesn't care whatsoever about the arguable crown jewel of one of their biggest series. This is yet another game kept alive by its awesome community, its hardly even playable otherwise.

The Sims 3:

[h1]Positives:[/h1]

+ Purchase a house for your family or build and design your own with hundreds of customisation options. Buy pools, decorative garden plants, televisions, computers, exercise machines, kitchen appliances, cars, toys for toddlers, sculptures, pet animals (DLC)....the list is huge! 
+ Work as a master criminal, a journalist, celebrity or even a detective + more! Attend University to further your studies and become a video game designer, sports agent or arts appraiser (DLC). Go travelling to Egypt, France and China (DLC). This game is packed with plenty to do.
+ Many different skills for your sims to level up, science, cooking, athleticism, logic, charisma etc, so you can have a very diverse gameplay experience.
+ Optional quests or objectives will become available from schooling, work and elsewhere, allowing you to participate in one-off opportunities with rewards.
+ Several neighbourhoods to play in, each with a unique layout.
+ There's a large amount of playtime in the Sims 3 for players of all sorts. I managed to get over 100 hours out of it.

[h1]Negatives:[/h1]

- Micromanagement is very unresponsive, Sims refuse to complete workplace objectives over and over and decide what they want to do themselves, instead of what you've told them. High free will means Sims react to basic needs problems like feeding a baby or bathing themselves, but it also results in ignoring your human commands repeatedly, which gets infuriating after a few hours.
- While I acknowledge graphics aren't a major focus of Sims gameplay, it could definitely be improved. Aesthetically, this game is disappointing.
- The game is quite expensive, even though it's now 8 years old (as of 20/02/2017). DLC is also pricey, so make sure you absolutely want this game before paying in full, or wait for a sale.
- Bad pathing by Sims, they don't interact with the environment well and get stuck in certain spots. Could be much smoother.  

- Despite the vastness of Sims 3, it can become boring after awhile. Once you build a mansion filled with the most luxurious objects money can buy and had a family, there's really not much else to do. This game has a cycle of repetition, whereby you continue to do the same tasks over and over, just in different ways and styles. Sure, the kids in your family grow up and you're able to control their lives, but it's like starting from scratch again, where's the sense of accomplishment in that? It's the balance between fun and repetitive content which the Sims 3 suffers from. There's a real conflict here, with the many facets of variability trying to shine, but then a monotonous feeling sometimes overshadowing it. 


Overall Score: 7.5/10
